chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام about a man who performs sajdah on a coarse cloth and a carpet. He said: There is no harm if he is in a state of taqiyyah.

key_terms.الْبِسَاطِ: a carpet or spread laid on the ground
key_terms.الْمِسْحِ: a coarse woven cloth or fabric used as a surface
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: taqiyyah; precautionary dissimulation due to circumstances of fear or constraint
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sajdah on a carpet or cloth during taqiyyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning sajdah on materials such as a coarse cloth or carpet. It states that doing so is permissible in a situation of taqiyyah, indicating a concession in worship when dissimulation or precaution is required.
